affectedSurfaces: native delegate harness invalidation and quarantine
workflow and loop agent-harness execution context
hypothesis: Routing the live scope-policy authority through KOTA-owned tool execution, while withholding it from native adapters and giving each native delegate the canonical child invalidation lifecycle, will stop and quarantine delegates on parent cancellation or restrictive authority revisions without weakening launch-time autonomy capping or native tool-control isolation.

metricsCompared.name: unsafe native delegate launch cases
metricsCompared.baseline: Native delegates launched from a one-time policy snapshot without a child AbortController or restrictive-policy subscription, and incomplete live context did not block launch.
metricsCompared.candidate: 0 of 1 incomplete-context cases reached the registered native harness; parent cancellation and restrictive revisions both stopped the active child through confirmed-stop quarantine.

metricsCompared.name: delegate invalidation lifecycle coverage
metricsCompared.baseline: The shared lifecycle existed for workflow callers but native delegate success, thrown failure, parent-abort, policy-abort, and listener-disposal paths had no focused coverage.
metricsCompared.candidate: 21 of 21 focused delegate, runner, routing, and hosted-policy tests passed across the required terminal and invalidation paths.

metricsCompared.name: shared harness and workflow regression coverage
metricsCompared.baseline: Live scope-policy authority was not carried through the nested delegate execution context.
metricsCompared.candidate: 70 of 70 broadened harness, loop, delegate, workflow-step, lifecycle, scope-policy, and Claude-adapter tests passed while native canUseTool and authority isolation remained enforced.

metricsCompared.name: static and repository policy gates
metricsCompared.baseline: No candidate result was available for the live native-delegate authority route.
metricsCompared.candidate: Type checking passed; 5 of 5 strict-types, root-layout, and core-boundary policy tests passed; Biome, task validation, staged diff checks, and hygiene passed.

rationale: The candidate closes a confirmed native-delegate authorization gap by requiring complete live invalidation context before launch, linking parent cancellation and restrictive authority revisions to one child controller, and activating the existing confirmed-stop native quarantine contract. Launch-time scope capping remains in place, live authority stays confined to KOTA-owned tool execution, and focused plus broadened validation passes with deterministic lifecycle cleanup.
